Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: [TO BE VERIFIED from TNAU/ICAR] Dark water-soaked lesions on leaves rapidly expanding into purplish-black spots, white fungal-like growth underneath leaf surfaces during humid weather.
Potato___Late_blight.treatment: [TO BE VERIFIED from TNAU/ICAR] Remove and destroy severely infected haulms/vines immediately. Apply recommended protective fungicides as per local agricultural university/extension guidelines.
Potato___Late_blight.prevention: [TO BE VERIFIED from TNAU/ICAR] Use certified disease-free seed tubers, ensure wide row spacing for good air circulation, avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation, and practice 2-3 year crop rotation.

Potato___healthy.symptoms: No visible disease symptoms. Foliage is vibrant green, firm, and actively growing without necrotic spots or lesions.
Potato___healthy.treatment: No disease treatment required. Continue balanced nutrition (NPK) and standard crop management.
Potato___healthy.prevention: Maintain scheduled scouting, proper hilling, weed management, and regular soil moisture monitoring.

Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: [TO BE VERIFIED from TNAU/ICAR] Concentric dark brown-to-black ring spots ('target board' pattern) on older lower leaves, leaf yellowing around lesions, premature defoliation.
Tomato___Early_blight.treatment: [TO BE VERIFIED from TNAU/ICAR] Prune and discard diseased lower leaves. Apply university-approved contact or systemic protective spray in accordance with local agronomist advisory.
Tomato___Early_blight.prevention: [TO BE VERIFIED from TNAU/ICAR] Apply organic mulch around plant bases to prevent soil splash, stake plants to elevate canopy, practice 3-year solanaceous crop rotation, and water at soil level.

Tomato___healthy.symptoms: Healthy leaf tissue. Clear green coloration with uniform foliage structure and absence of chlorosis or fungal spots.
Tomato___healthy.treatment: No disease treatment required. Continue balanced fertilization and adequate hydration.
Tomato___healthy.prevention: Ensure adequate spacing, sanitize pruning tools, inspect weekly for early pest/disease vectors, and maintain balanced soil nutrients.
